text: The CDC-to-Flow example uses an `after insert` event trigger and requires bulkification because the trigger can receive a list of events. (low confidence)

text: Salesforce documents Flow action transaction control starting in Winter ’26. Record-triggered flows can apply it on asynchronous or scheduled paths, but not the immediate path. A callout with pending operations fails if the action always continues in the current transaction. (low confidence)
keywords: Salesforce Apex CDC triggers and Flow outbound alert delivery

text: Lightning after-save Flow triggers can initiate SOAP outbound messages. Salesforce generates a WSDL for the external listener and dispatches messages through a local background process. (low confidence)

text: Apex change-event triggers execute outside the transaction that published the change event, but use synchronous Apex governor limits. The default running identity is Automated Process; PlatformEventSubscriberConfig can override the running user and batch size. (low confidence)
keywords: Salesforce Apex CDC triggers and Flow outbound alert delivery

text: Bulkify CDC trigger handlers: Salesforce’s example warns that the trigger receives a list of events, and the developer guide documents a maximum batch of 2,000 event messages. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)

text: For record-triggered Flow actions, transaction controls apply to asynchronous or scheduled paths, not the immediate path. With Let the flow decide, a callout with pending work commits the current transaction and runs in a new one; Always continue in current transaction instead fails in that situation. With Let the flow decide, debugging keeps the action in the current transaction. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)
keywords: Salesforce Apex CDC triggers and Flow outbound alert delivery

text: SOAP outbound messages can be initiated by an after-save Flow. Delivery uses a local scheduled background process and OutboundMessage records, separate from the asynchronous Apex queue; executing the Flow action does not send the message synchronously. (low confidence)
keywords: Salesforce Apex CDC triggers and Flow outbound alert delivery

text: Asynchronous Flow execution has no SLA and can have unpredictable wait times. An asynchronous path keeps work off the initiating transaction’s critical path, but does not establish a fixed alert-delivery deadline. (low confidence)
keywords: Salesforce Apex CDC triggers and Flow outbound alert delivery

text: For outbound Apex callouts initiated from a data-change trigger, Salesforce’s integration guide requires asynchronous execution from the initiating event. The async decision guide recommends Queueable Apex over future methods and warns that finite asynchronous threads can delay outbound integrations. (medium confidence)
keywords: Salesforce Apex CDC triggers and Flow outbound alert delivery

text: Salesforce’s January 2021 CDC-to-Flow example uses an Apex change-event trigger to copy header and changed-field values into a Flow-compatible input class and invoke an autolaunched Flow. keywords: Salesforce Apex CDC triggers and Flow outbound alert delivery

text: CDC event processing decouples work from the original database transaction; Salesforce’s example uses the change event rather than the original object to start its Apex-to-Flow bridge. (low confidence)

text: Outbound-message retries can arrive out of order or more than once. Check notification IDs before processing. keywords: Salesforce Apex CDC triggers and Flow outbound alert delivery

text: Asynchronous Salesforce processing has no completion-time SLA or consistent latency guarantee. An external case alert design therefore needs an explicit latency expectation and monitoring. (low confidence)
keywords: Salesforce Apex CDC triggers and Flow outbound alert delivery

text: If a SOAP outbound-message endpoint is unavailable, Salesforce retries delivery and drops the message after 24 hours of unsuccessful delivery. This is bounded retry, not indefinite guaranteed delivery. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)
